title: Mary and the saints
hook: a daily Marian prayer and a saint for the year
tomorrow: what happens to a rule when life breaks your routine?

segments.voice: This week built a rule piece by piece: a book, your people, a guide, a fast, a portion, and yesterday's line, holy leisure. One more piece, and it's about who walks with you.

The first day somewhere new: a cafeteria, a locker room, an office, eyes scanning for one familiar face. Who walks in with you? John's Gospel tells of a moment at the cross. Jesus sees his mother, and the disciple he loves standing beside her, and gives them to each other. To her: "Woman, behold thy son." To him: "Behold thy mother."
screen: `ONE FAMILIAR FACE.` → `AT THE CROSS.` → `BEHOLD THY MOTHER.`

segments.voice: John adds: "And from that hour, the disciple took her to his own." Catholics hear that as a gift to every disciple, a mother for the road. So a rule for life often keeps one short daily prayer to Mary, short enough never to skip: a Hail Mary in the car, the Angelus at noon, a decade before sleep. Then the saints. The letter to the Hebrews says believers have "so great a cloud of witnesses over our head," people who ran this race before and now surround the ones still running. Catholics honor them and ask their prayers; worship belongs to God alone. One to tell a friend: some Catholic families keep a custom of drawing a saint's name at the new year, and letting that saint, not the one they'd have picked, keep them company all year. A stranger who becomes a friend. Now the week comes back: six pieces of a rule, in a round.
screen: `BEHOLD THY MOTHER.` · `A DAILY PRAYER TO MARY.` · `A CLOUD OF WITNESSES.` · `A SAINT FOR THE YEAR.` · then, large: `COMPANY FOR THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: If you pray, say one Hail Mary out loud, slowly, as if someone were listening beside you. If you don't, say aloud the name of one saint or one person of faith whose story you'd like to know better this year. Let that name sit with you while the time runs.
Mary and the saints. A mother given from the cross, and a cloud of witnesses who ran the road first.
The line to keep: company for the road, a mother and a saint who walk in with you. See you next week.

howItsDone: Many Catholics pray a short daily prayer to Mary, such as the Hail Mary, the Angelus or a decade of the rosary; some families draw a patron saint's name at the new year to learn about and pray with through the year.

chat.meaning: Saints are company for the road. Drawing one for the year is a custom for getting to know a friend you didn't choose.

Hail Mary.meaning: a prayer to Mary built from the angel's and Elizabeth's greetings in Luke

Angelus.meaning: a short prayer recalling the angel's message to Mary, said at noon

decade.meaning: one stretch of the rosary: an Our Father, Hail Marys, a Glory Be

Hebrews.meaning: a New Testament letter about faith and Christ as high priest

witnesses.meaning: people who saw and testified; here, the faithful who went before

notes: John 19:26–27 and Hebrews 12:1 quoted from Douay-Rheims (Challoner); confirm exact wording.
'Catholics hear that as a gift to every disciple' (John 19:27 read as Mary given to the Church): a traditional Catholic reading, voiced as such. Confirm.
Saint-for-the-year custom (drawing a name at the new year) is described as a custom some families keep, not a Church practice. Confirm framing.
Angelus 'at noon': traditionally prayed morning, noon and evening; the lesson names noon only. Confirm.
